kind: manual visual annotations in the 1280x960 fixture derivative; (col, row) with row 0 at the top
annotated: 2026-09-23, from 2x crops with a 20 px row grid (scripts/measure_lookout_locus.py --crops reproduces them)

crest_wave_a.role: b: the active breaking crest carrying two riders; the top edge of the green face, seaward-most unbroken water of this wave
crest_wave_a.note: left of col 640 the wave is unbroken swell nearer the camera; it breaks from col ~1050 rightward

riders_wave_a.role: b: the two riders on wave A (dark marks on the face just under the lip)

peel_head_wave_a.role: b: where the green face meets the whitewater (the zipper head) on wave A

crest_wave_b.role: d: the outer unbroken line - the next wave of the set, green face, breaking from col ~1130 rightward
crest_wave_b.note: not discernible left of col ~700 at this exposure

peel_head_wave_b.role: d: green-to-whitewater transition on wave B

lineup_cluster.role: c: sitting surfers (2-10 px dark marks) - the lineup, sampled

outer_dark_band.role: reference only: a dark shore-parallel band far outside both waves (kelp canopy or wind shadow); not a break, excluded from the residual

inshore_foam_field.role: reference only: residual foam and sun glitter inshore, no crest, no coherent seaward edge; excluded from the residual

whitewater_auto.method: luma > 195 and HSV saturation < 60 inside ROI rows [340, 520), all columns; then per column the seaward-most (minimum) masked row, split into wave B (rows < 392) and wave A (rows >= 392)
whitewater_auto.why_this_roi: above row 340 is sky/cloud (white, unsaturated - the same signature as foam); below row 520 is sun glitter on the inside water, also white

distinguishing_break_from_reform: Both whitewater bands terminate leftward in a clean green face carrying a rider (wave A) or a clean green line (wave B); a reformed inner bore has no unbroken face ahead of it. The inshore foam field at rows 560-720 is the residue of earlier waves - texture without a crest - and is the only candidate for an inner reform; it is annotated and excluded.
